eligibility.quote: That said, I see exactly what you mean about the loaned APIs.  They do not work like that; once the memory is returned to the underlying middleware, they should be considered invalid.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: the Docker reproducer, startup exception, and maintainer-confirmed ownership mismatch establish the defect. E2: rclcpp retains a pointer to memory loaned by a separate RMW provider and returns that loan before its retained pointer is finished. The boundary includes lifetime/ownership, not merely the initially correct clock value. Correct behavior depends on the provider's loan contract; non-loaned APIs do not exhibit this lifetime behavior. This is an interface failure even though the consumer-side executor needs changing. E3: PAIR through the loan/return API, via rcl.

supporting_evidence.quote: And in point of fact, if you use the non-loaned APIs, it works exactly as you expect; the object can live beyond the scope of the callback, assuming the callback takes a reference.

missed_conditions.quote: In the above code the excecutor creates dummy **shared_ptr** with empty destructor and loads the loaned message, than calls the subscription callbacks (`cache_last_msg`) and frees the memory, altought the shared_ptr is still kept by `ClockState`.
missed_conditions.reason: A loaned-buffer lifetime/ownership precondition is violated. It is not an encoding, ROS message type, clock-unit, permission, or resource-claim mismatch. These are proposed inventory entries because the specification supplies none.

resolution.quote: We disabled loans by default via https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/pull/2335 and https://github.com/ros2/rcl/pull/1110
resolution.reason: There is a documented workaround and backport, not an absent resolution. The closing account does not identify both tested unit revisions, so it does not meet observed. Disabling subscription loaning avoids the failure; it does not prove repaired ownership semantics when loaning is re-enabled.

supporting_evidence.quote: The above works around the issue.  There is one remaining issue here, which is to re-enable loaned messages along with shared_ptrs.

notes: The chosen composition is rclcpp with the loan-providing RMW, not a clock publisher with a subscriber whose incoming clock value is intrinsically wrong. The separately discussed MessagePoolMemoryStrategy defect is a different allocation composition and is not added as another condition here.
